- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged high — reduce forecast by 2–5% in the following 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model often fails to recognize it — adjust downward by 1–4% for next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (first 5–7 days) — apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misjudges turning points — use sentiment swing as trigger for 1–2% adjustment in direction of sentiment shift.
